entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Furius Philus was a Roman statesman who became consul of ancient Rome in 136 BC, marking a pivotal moment in the Scipionic Circle's influence on Roman politics.

Philus's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the Scipionic Circle, a group of prominent Romans who shaped Roman policy and diplomacy during the 2nd century BC. He was particularly close to Scipio Aemilianus, a renowned general and statesman who played a crucial role in the Second Punic War.

Philus's leadership and diplomatic skills were instrumental in maintaining Roman power and influence in the Mediterranean region. His actions and decisions had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of Roman history and leaving a lasting legacy in the annals of ancient Rome.

Despite the passage of time, Lucius Furius Philus remains an enigmatic figure, shrouded in the shadows of history. His life and achievements continue to captivate historians and scholars, offering a glimpse into the complexities of ancient Roman politics and the enduring power of human influence.
